paste_notes: This team does its best to utilize the Doom Desire Jirachi to pressure the most common status absorbers, Blissey, Swampert, and Starmie, with its combination of Doom Desire, Thunder, and HP Grass. Blissey supports the paraspam and is a fantastic special wall vs things Jirachi can't handle, and Restzap frees up Blissey's moveslots. Wish on Jirachi supports all of Zapdos, Claydol, and BKCTar to do their jobs better, and BKCTar is the primary beneficiary of the paraspam. Spikes is good for pressuring the common status absorbers and makes many attacks 2hkos and preserve the high bulk on the team. Celebi is a slight problem, but Roar + Sleep Talk Zapdos, Drill Peck Skarmory, and Flame + Ice on Blissey make the matchup winnable especially with how good the matchup is into many common celebi cores (such as Unemployed 6 or Aerobi) where they struggle with some combination of Jirachi, BKCTar, and RestZap.

paste_notes:
Gen 3 OU
Fun squad built around endgame Scizor. 
Breloom lures and chips fliers for Scizor. It also provides early game momentum and a soft check to DD Tar.
Metagross provides a Rock resist and solid switchin to Aerodactyl. 
Snorlax provides the team with an interim measure against special attackers like Starmie.
Tyranitar traps Gengar to help Breloom, Gyarados and Scizor to sweep. It also helps in the Moltres matchup.
Jolly HP Rock Gyarados provides a nice Aerodactyl and Jolteon lure.
The team is a bit flaws, but pretty fun to use.

thread_title: ADV OU Creative Sets, Synergistic Cores, and Concepts

paste_notes:
Was making sets and thought of doing Download (Forgot Download was gen 4+) But decided that I liked the idea of offensive Porgyon 2. So I made this team around it. An Offensive Team, with Porgyon 2 nice for Dug as well. Since this team can struggle with dug.

Ttar lead cause Mix Ttar is really awesome and I like using it. Don't like too many other Ttar sets too much but this set is really good.

Porgyon 2 of course, special attacking Hp Grass for Pert since that can really be a sturggle for this team. With Max Special Attack it is cleaving a hole and its 105SPA is not even that bad. Ice Beam and Thunderbolt both hit extra hard and recover to you know recover and take advantage of porgyon 2 nice natural bulk.

Salamance is a endgamer sweeper, DD set I didn't like DD before this team but now I actually enjoy it a lot more. With this team around it I feel like I can save it most of the time then +1 on something force something out. Sometimes though this does kinda become a mid game wall breaker for Aero.

Speaking of Aero, don't like Choice Band that much. Its strong and fast but I get to pick one move. In some matches I do wish I had band however, I'd rather have the ability to flip movesets around whenever it is needed. Hp Bug for Celbi over Hp Flying, though this does make Breloom and fighters kinda scary. So its a pick your poison.

Dugtrio, Admant for the power boost. I wanna be able to cleave things. 339 speed still outspeeds most targets. note, most. This team really hates Starmie so if you wanna just make sure starmie does down after you sac something to it, Jolly instead. 


Metagross as another wallbreaker, Explosion is scary for everything. This was offensivly one of the weaker mons for the team but it also provides a backbone and can soak usually at least one physically hit then boom or kill with mash or something. Like a +1 Mence or something. So it and Porgyon 2 kinda serve as the semi tanky mons just in case I need to switch them into something deadly, they don't get folded usually be any one single move.

Lead with Ttar, make switches and find opening, break them open with Metagross, Salamance, Aerodactyl or Porgyon 2. Use Dug when you get the chance to trap. Save Aero or Salamance for the end game to sweep. That is the simple game plan.

thread_title: A deep look at Rain Offense

paste_notes:
Ludicolo: Lum Berry because it's usually the target of TWaves, especially as a lead.
Kingdra: Dual rain sweepers because it's hyper offense. There's also 4 physical attackers in the back, meaning you'll get your chance to handle Blissey (hopefully, could be wrong). Petaya for EndPetaya (setting rain allows it to be viable). Sub for activating Petaya and evading status.
Heracross: Sub for evading status and activating Salac. Reversal because the goal is to get to close to 1 HP and get off 150/200 BP Reversals. Swarm to compliment low HP. Rain allows both of these to be viable imo.
Snorlax: Offensive because Idrk how to use Snorlax besides going guns blazing max Atk and investing the rest in Def.
Dugtrio: I've heard that SdDef variants of Duggy would work well vs. Blissey, and maybe replace Aerial Ace with Beat Up?
Metagross: I've heard bulky variants might be better. I invested a little in Def but this could probably be optimized

Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense) [Peak 1436 ELO]

paste_notes: CB Metagross is to eliminate any wall that is in/switches in T1. I use Boom 90% of the time. T2 I switch to Ludi to set up Rain, or to try and Pump Ttar if it's in. If Ttar gets revealed later, I usually sack a mon and then trap it with ScreechLiechi Dugtrio, a set that I've come to love for its ability to survive an Ice Beam/HP Ice/EQ from the mons it wants to trap and proceed to decimate them with the lowered defense and sometimes Liechi Atk boost. Kingdra is there to put even more pressure on the opponent after Ludi is gone, if they don't have a Ludi check that also checks Dra (which is usually the case, there's another purpose, too): If that's the case, it can still serve a purpose later in the game to clean, or set Rain again to enable Hera's SalacReversal set. HP Electric is for Gyara, a mon that this team struggles with if it doesn't get Boomed on. Rock Slide is on Dugtrio because it can get the surprise Slide on a switch in if it EQs/HP Bugs without using Screech. Snorlax is to Boom on more walls to enable Ludi/Dra/Hera. Or it can Focus Punch and switch out. I usually don't use Return or EQ unless most of the opponent's team is gone and they don't have any resists. Last is the most devastating member of the team, Hera: with Rain, it can get the Salac boost and not worry about Sand chip each turn. Swarm Megahorn/Reversal does great against most threats not named Salamence/Gyarados. With +2 Atk it can even OHKO some Gengar builds.
paste_title: [Gen 3] OU: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense)
thread_title: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense) [Peak 1436 ELO]

paste_notes: The goal of this team is to get rid of walls like Skarmory, Suicune, and Blissey early with dual Boom and tech Dug, and then wreak havoc on the Special side with Kingdra/Ludicolo and on the Physical side with Heracross. Rain Dance is to ensure the Rain sweepers outspeed the base 130s after the Swift Swim boost, and Lum because they're Para bait and can set up a Rain Dance in the face of TWavers. Rain Dance is also to ensure Heracross can keep the Salac boost, instead of dropping dead to Sand.
paste_title: [Gen 3] OU: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense)
thread_title: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense) [Peak 1436 ELO]

paste_notes: The goal of this team is twofold: either get in the dual Special sweepers Kingdra/Ludicolo and obliterate physDef teams with Rain spam, or get in the Physical (albeit gimmicky) sweeper Heracross to demolish non-defensive teams. BPZapDug helps take out key opponents (mainly Blissey) systematically. Max Atk Gengar allows you to finish off bulky Pokemon with a follow-up Dug trap.
paste_title: [Gen 3] OU: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense) [Peak 1436 ELO]
thread_title: Riders on the Storm (Rain Hyper Offense) [Peak 1436 ELO]

paste_notes: The goal of this team is twofold; get in your Special breaker Dra, or get in your Physical breaker Hera. Both can sweep once you get rid of their checks/counters. To do that, I've employed ZapDug (with SpDef Dug able to sponge a hit from Ice Beam), CBGross, and Lonely BoomGar. SubDos allows you to Sub T1 and possibly (virtually) win the Special offense game on the spot if they hard switch to Blissey; you can then eat a hit, do 60-70% with Beat Up (or more due to its high crit ratio), and then survive untouched, even by Counter. CBGross's goal is to get rid of bulky mons so your two wallbreakers can setup without getting KOd, first (or phased). It's a great lure for all the walls if you click Boom early, or it can win in the late game Mashing. Lonely BoomGar is something I'd proud to have come up with that lures in Blissey and then OHKOs standard variants. This is helpful for Dra as well. Last is the setup wallbreakers/sweepers, Dra/Hera. Dra sets up with Rain Dance, sponges a hit with its great defenses (only weak to Dragon), and then proceeds to decimate with Surf. Hera requires a bit more thought; you try to get in Salac range, while also trying to get a SD off. Then you can break through/sweep with your nuclear Swarm-boosted Megahorns or >= 100 BP Reversals. This team has been my most consistent team on ladder, and I hope you enjoy using it!
